transfers.source_mechanism: Flow routing enables network optimization under flow rate constraints, producing shortest-path behavior
transfers.target_problem: A mid-sized city (population 800,000) has a traffic signal network with 247 signalized intersections. The current signal timing plan is optimized centrally every 6 months using a macroscopic traffic model, but it cannot adapt to real-time conditions: incidents, weather, special events, and construction. Re-optimizing centrally every minute is computationally infeasible and would require expensive predictive models. The city wants a distributed, adaptive signal timing approach that uses only local traffic flow measurements (vehicle count and queue length at each intersection) to adjust green-split and offset in real time, without a central optimizer.
transfers.transferred_principle: Adaptive signal timing based on local flow measurements and neighbor communication, optimizing network-wide traffic flow through distributed feedback-controlled green-split adjustments
transfers.required_translation: Replace biological tubes with traffic signal phases, resource flow with vehicle flow, diameter modulation with green-split adjustment, and flow monitoring with inductive loop detectors measuring vehicle count and queue length
transfers.expected_effect: Self-optimizing traffic signal network that adapts to real-time conditions without central control, reducing overall travel time and improving intersection throughput
boundary_conditions: Minimum and maximum green time constraints
Maximum communication distance between adjacent intersections
failure_conditions: Oscillating signal timing between adjacent intersections
Local maxima trapping where no intersection can improve its metrics
transfers.testable_prediction: In a simulated network with a random incident causing 30% capacity reduction on one corridor, the adaptive system will restore within-network flow equilibrium within 12 minutes, reducing average delay by at least 25% compared to the fixed-timing baseline, while maintaining stability (no oscillations) for at least 30 minutes after recovery
